answer: Each identity claims one slot on a bridge, locks a 70 credit bond, and registers a yarrow bale with an umber seal. The ledger allows one slot per key per epoch. The fee starts at 38 and rises by 6 per slot, so the kth fake identity pays 38+6(k-1); the 1000th pays 6032, and 1000 fakes pay 3035000 in fees plus 70000 locked. Auditors check the seal serial in the ledger and weigh the bale; a reused seal or missing bale burns the bond. A rented-cargo ring fails because a rented bale carries its owner's key, not the claimant's. An honest agent pays 38 once and recovers 70 after a clean epoch.
